subject: zoology
question_text: List out the characters shared by chordates and echinoderms.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.55, VSAQ 107). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. TEXT BEYOND THE BOOK: the book prints the three names only; the one-line meanings are authored.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Deuterostome condition
steps.margin_note: Two shared characters here, one line each for the name and one for the meaning.
lines: The blastopore of the embryo becomes the anus,
and the mouth is formed later as a new opening.
Cleavage of the egg is radial and
steps.why: Both groups are deuterostomes, so the earliest events of the embryo run the same way in both — and it is these embryonic characters, not the adult body, that place echinoderms next to chordates.
common_mistakes: Writing that the blastopore becomes the mouth. That is the protostome condition.
Calling the cleavage spiral and determinate. That is again the protostome pattern.
steps.memory_tip: Deutero means second: the mouth is the SECOND opening to form.

steps.label: Enterocoelom
steps.margin_note: One boxed line holds all three names; then explain only the coelom.
lines: The coelom of both groups is an enterocoelom.
It is formed from pouches of the archenteron,
the embryonic gut, so the mesoderm and the
steps.why: The third shared character is the way the body cavity is built, and it follows from the same embryo: the gut wall itself gives out the pouches that become the coelom.
common_mistakes: Calling it a schizocoelom. A schizocoelom is split out of solid mesoderm; an enterocoelom grows out of the gut.
Naming only two characters. The question asks for the shared list, so give all three.
steps.memory_tip: Three shared points, all from the embryo: blastopore, cleavage, coelom.

insider_note: The examiner is looking for the three embryonic words — deuterostome, radial and indeterminate, enterocoelom; adult characters such as the water vascular system earn nothing here.
